newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Low stocks to underpin soybean prices in 97-Safras.
newsitem.headline: Low stocks to underpin soybean prices in 97-Safras.

text.p: World soybean prices should remain firm, yet volatile, in 1997 as low stocks are likely to keep the market sharply sensitive to any drops in supply, independent consultants Safras e Mercado said.
"There is even a possibility for a still better market than in 1996, if there is a harvest problem in any important producing country," Safras said in its weekly report.
World soybean production will rise to 132 million tonnes in 1996/97 from 124.4 million tonnes in 1995/96, Safras forecast.

Without major swings in weather conditions, the tendency was for prices to remain relatively stable until the end of March, when the U.S. forecast for planted area for the 1997/98 harvest is released, the report said.
A likely rise in U.S. planted area was expected to push prices lower, but concerns about the North American weather could underpin the market from then on, it added.
